full_name: Singapore AI Safety Institute (Digital Trust Centre)
mission: Singapore's AISI does technical testing of AI — especially multilingual/multicultural testing and agentic AI testing — often jointly with other institutes in the international network. It also studies AI's societal effects (such as emotional dependency and cognitive offloading) and convenes the 'Singapore Consensus' on global AI safety research priorities.

key_work.title: The 2026 Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities
key_work.plain_summary: Outcome of the second International Scientific Exchange on AI Safety (May 2026), with 100+ contributors from 13 countries. It lists top technical safety research problems, with new focus on societal resilience and on managing increasingly autonomous AI agents.

key_work.title: The Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities (2025)
key_work.plain_summary: Organises safety research into three areas in a 'defence-in-depth' model: building trustworthy systems (Development), evaluating risks (Assessment), and monitoring/intervening after deployment (Control).

key_work.title: Moonshot (open-source evaluation tool) and joint testing reports
key_work.plain_summary: Singapore's open-source LLM testing tool, used in network joint testing of multilingual agents, plus reports with Japan, Korea and Canada on multilingual benchmarks, data-leakage by agents and LLM-judge consistency.

status_note: the Digital Trust Centre (set up June 2022 at NTU with S$50m) was designated Singapore's AI Safety Institute on 22 May 2024; works in partnership with IMDA.

warnings.text: AI can fail in ways that only show up in non-English languages and cultures.
Increasingly autonomous AI agents can leak data during routine tasks and raise new risk-management problems.
AI may foster emotional dependency and cognitive offloading.

recommendations.text: Test models across languages and cultures, not only in English.
Prioritise research on agent risk management and societal resilience (2026 Consensus).
Use a defence-in-depth approach: develop, assess and control AI systems.
